A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TopoTune and GCCNs. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable through extraction and rendering, and corresponding methods, experiments, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCCN benchmark evaluations, comparisons with existing CCNNs, and analyses of neighborhood choices and parameter efficiency.

after.justification: v3 retains these original evaluations and adds measured training times in Appendix H, Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: The GCCN pipeline, Equation 8, and TopoTune pseudocode remain unchanged. However, v3 newly defines an auxiliary k-CCNN architecture with feature updates on k-sets of cells (Appendix B.3.3, Equation 11), used in its expressivity argument rather than the reported benchmark implementation.

E1.justification: The same eight main benchmarks, simplicial/cellular liftings, hypergraph comparisons, and existing Amazon-ratings appendix plot are retained. Labeling ZINC as a subset clarifies existing coverage; its reported dataset statistics are unchanged.

E2.justification: The reported comparator sets remain unchanged: best CCNNs by domain, single-Hasse-graph alternatives, and SCCN/CWN counterparts. The new timing tables use these same comparisons. TopoBenchmarkX becoming TopoBenchmark does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds training-time evaluation on a single NVIDIA A30 GPU, explicitly including on-the-fly graph expansion. The existing predictive evaluations retain their splits, metrics, architecture search, optimization settings, and stopping procedures.

E4.justification: v3 adds an empirical computational-cost analysis comparing training times across models and datasets, extending the existing parameter-efficiency analysis. The neighborhood comparisons and performance-versus-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed/split evaluations and performance uncertainty, including the same one-standard-deviation highlighting. The added timing results extend the existing ± reporting practice without announcing changed repetition counts or new statistical tests.

E6.justification: Predictive scores, parameter counts, and existing plotted results are unchanged, but Tables 6–7 add extensive training-time results. For example, cellular GCCN with GIN takes 3301 ± 440 seconds on ZINC versus 228 ± 44 for the reported best CCNN. These are newly reported timings, not a cross-version performance change.

T1.justification: v1's short expressivity-preservation argument is replaced by neighborhood-based homomorphism/isomorphism definitions, CCWL and k-CCWL tests, k-CCNN constructions, multiple propositions, and a separation example supporting strict superiority. Appendix C adds FLOP derivations. The new Proposition B.10 construction contains an unresolved feature-indexing gap.

C1.justification: Although the abstract's principal framework and benchmark claims remain, v3 strengthens the central expressivity result from preservation to strict superiority over CCNNs (Proposition 4.3). Its introduction and conclusion also newly position the contributions as addressing seven of eleven identified TDL open problems.

C2.justification: v3 materially qualifies the computational-efficiency discussion: fewer parameters do not ensure faster training, and larger-dataset slowdowns are attributed to on-the-fly expansion. Appendix E.2 newly discusses benchmark selection and memory/computational bottlenecks from cycle detection and clique enumeration on large or dense graphs.

D1.justification: v3 newly states that node features construct edge/face features, identifies A30 timing hardware, and changes the repository location. Code-release wording becomes inconsistent: the introduction promises scripts upon acceptance, while Section 5 says they are provided. Most implementation and hyperparameter details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially extends positioning through explicit connections to TDL open problems and higher-order GNN/WL theory, adding works including Morris et al. (2019, 2023), Grohe (2017), and Kiefer (2020). It also reframes the comparison with graph simulations around lost topological distinctions and cites scalable-lifting research.

P1.justification: The main section sequence, abstract, and much of the core exposition remain. v3 revises motivation and results prose, reorganizes discussion headings, renames TopoBenchmarkX, adds explanatory background, and reorganizes the appendices, including moving the SCCN/CWN comparison out of the main text.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, relocates the counterpart-comparison table, adds Figures 6–9 and timing Tables 6–7, and marks per-rank choices in Figure 5's legend. Existing plots are retained. Algorithm 1 also acquires erroneous all-zero line numbering.

improvement.justification: The timing benchmarks and scalability limitations improve practical transparency beyond v1's parameter-count comparisons. However, the strengthened expressivity claim relies on Proposition B.10: Equation 12 accesses H^l(σ,u) for neighboring k-sets u that need not contain σ, although those feature blocks are defined only for sets containing σ. This unresolved gap affects a central new argument. With clear reporting benefits but uncertain support for the stronger theoretical contribution, a reliable overall quality direction cannot be established.
